intent.raw: Spec and design the implementation and integration of auth with BodyWar.
intent.objective: Author a governed define/design/plan packet for integrating BodyWar/TROQAR with @domainspec/auth-user-management without executing implementation.
intent.operator_sentence: Use invoke to spec and design BodyWar auth integration.

technique_overlays.trigger: BodyWar imports non-existent package browser/OAuth helpers while the current auth package boundary excludes HTTP, cookies, OAuth, Strava, and UI.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Artifacts must distinguish shared auth package ownership from BodyWar-owned browser, Strava, profile, and HTTP adapter ownership.

technique_overlays.trigger: Real VPS and Strava production proof are blocked, but local compile and E2E integration can proceed.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: The work-pack must select a first SWU that repairs the package/app auth boundary and recomposes into local E2E and later deployment proof.

technique_overlays.trigger: Strava tokens, OAuth codes, session cookies, friend activity evidence, and production secrets are protected state.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Protected state must remain out of tracked artifacts, and operator-gated production proof must stay blocked.

steps.name: Build bounded auth integration context
stop_conditions: Stop if live auth package exports contradict the selected integration boundary.
Stop if protected secrets or private provider payloads are required for planning.

steps.name: Author BodyWar auth integration spec
stop_conditions: Stop if the spec assigns BodyWar product adapters to the shared auth package.
Stop if the spec requires real deployment credentials.

steps.name: Author six-view integration design
stop_conditions: Stop if the design cannot separate package auth from BodyWar cookies, CSRF, Strava, profile, and HTTP routes.
Stop if generated migration ownership cannot be represented.

steps.name: Author layering and executable work-pack
stop_conditions: Stop if no SWU can repair the current compile failure before deployment work.
Stop if any SWU needs real Strava secrets, real VPS access, or friend activity consent.

steps.name: Validate smallest unit and prepare handoff
stop_conditions: Stop if the selected first SWU does not recompose into the BodyWar auth integration design.
Stop if deployment proof is treated as available without operator decisions.

gates.condition: Shared auth package and BodyWar adapter ownership are separated.
No real Strava tokens, OAuth codes, production secrets, or friend activity payloads are written into artifacts.
PostgreSQL setup uses Drizzle schema and Drizzle Kit generated migrations.
Real deployment and real Strava/friend evidence remain blocked until existing operator decisions are resolved.

boundaries.contract: Auth package owns core auth use cases, repositories, token codec, and generated auth migrations; BodyWar owns cookies, CSRF, Strava OAuth, provider token custody, profile, and HTTP routes.
No real deploy, DNS, Strava production callback, or friend activity use occurs before the operator supplies private decisions and consent.

authority.lifecycle: invoke authors artifacts; task-session owns execution
authority.validation: BodyWar and auth package npm checks plus E2E scripts
authority.memory: no memory promotion from this dispatch
authority.promotion: no production readiness promotion without deployment receipt

state_namespaces.write_policy: May contain specs, designs, plans, redacted receipts, and placeholders only.
Never write into tracked artifacts; use VPS or CI secret store.
Persist server-side only, encrypted/protected, and expose redacted summaries.

promotion_guardrails: This dispatch does not promote production readiness.
This dispatch does not approve real Strava credential handling.
This dispatch does not promote glossary or architecture corrections into canonical docs without a later SWU.
